description: This chapter focuses on divisibility and common properties of numbers. Understanding these concepts is essential for speed and accuracy in competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Before understanding HCF and LCM, it is necessary to understand factors and multiples.

key_concepts.explanation: Any number that divides a given number exactly without leaving a remainder is called a factor of that number.
The result obtained by multiplying a number by an integer is called a multiple of that number.
The process of expressing a number as a product of its prime numbers.

sections.title: Highest Common Factor (HCF)
sections.description: HCF is the largest number that can exactly divide two or more given numbers.

key_concepts.explanation: Also known as Greatest Common Divisor (GCD). It is the largest among the common factors of the given numbers.

steps.title: Prime Factorization Method
steps.detail: Write all given numbers as powers of their prime factors.

steps.title: Identify Common Factors
steps.detail: Choose only the prime numbers that are common to all the given numbers.

steps.title: Lowest Power Calculation
steps.detail: Take the lowest power of the common prime numbers and multiply them. The product is the HCF.

cases.condition: When to use the Division Method
results: Use when numbers are very large and finding prime factors is difficult.
Continue dividing successively; the last divisor obtained is the HCF.

sections.title: Least Common Multiple (LCM)
sections.description: LCM is the smallest number that is exactly divisible by two or more given numbers.

key_concepts.explanation: It is the smallest common multiple among all the multiples of the given numbers.

steps.title: Prime Factorization
steps.detail: Break down all given numbers into their prime factors.

steps.title: List All Factors
steps.detail: Include all the prime factors present, regardless of whether they are common or not.

steps.title: Highest Power Calculation
steps.detail: Take the highest power of each prime factor and multiply them. The result is the LCM.

sections.title: Important Properties and Formulas
sections.description: There is a direct relationship between HCF and LCM that helps solve exam problems quickly.

equations: First Number * Second Number = HCF * LCM

results: Their LCM is equal to their product (LCM = A * B).

cases.condition: When one number is a multiple of the other
results: The smaller number is the HCF.
The larger number is the LCM.

sections.title: HCF and LCM of Fractions and Decimals
sections.description: There are special rules for finding the HCF and LCM of fractions and decimal numbers.

equations: HCF of Fractions = HCF of Numerators / LCM of Denominators
LCM of Fractions = LCM of Numerators / HCF of Denominators

steps.title: Adjusting Decimal Numbers
steps.detail: First, make the number of decimal places equal in all given numbers by adding zeros.

steps.title: Calculate without Decimals
steps.detail: Ignore the decimal points and calculate the HCF or LCM of the numbers as whole integers.

steps.title: Placing the Decimal Point
steps.detail: In the final result, place the decimal point from the right after the same number of places as established in step 1.
